headline: Houthis Take Perim Island, Tightening Grip on Bab el-Mandeb Shipping Route
seoTitle: Houthis Take Perim Island in Bab el-Mandeb | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have taken strategic Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, adding new pressure on a critical Red Sea shipping route.
deck: The capture of Perim, also known as Mayun, gives Houthi forces a new foothold inside the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as Middle East shipping and oil routes face mounting pressure.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: U.S.–Iran Fire Resumes as Oil Prices Jump
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported renewed U.S.–Iran attacks and rising concern around the Strait of Hormuz, Iran-aligned Houthi forces have captured Perim Island inside the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, creating a new material risk around another major regional shipping corridor.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have taken Perim Island, also known as Mayun, inside Yemen’s Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to reporting independently corroborated by Reuters and the Associated Press.

Reuters reported on September 11 that four Yemeni government sources said Houthi forces had reached the strategic island after government forces withdrew. AP separately reported that the capture was confirmed by a senior military official with Yemen’s internationally recognized government and by a Houthi official.

The Houthis also advanced through nearby areas on Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including Dhubab. Houthi forces have said maritime navigation remains safe for companies other than Saudi vessels, but control of the island does not by itself establish that the group controls or has closed the entire Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News’ August 31 report focused on renewed U.S.–Iran attacks, higher oil prices and risk around the Strait of Hormuz.

The new development is a Houthi territorial gain inside Bab el-Mandeb itself. That puts an Iran-aligned force on a strategically located island at the southern entrance to the Red Sea while the wider Middle East conflict is already disrupting other energy and shipping routes.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Bab el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea. It is a key route for vessels moving between Asia, the Middle East and Europe through the Suez Canal.

Shipping through the area had already been reduced by years of Houthi attacks and threats. The route has taken on added importance during the current Middle East conflict because Saudi Arabia has relied more heavily on Red Sea export routes while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been severely disrupted.
Reuters also reported that Yemeni government forces intend to try to retake captured areas. The territorial and maritime situation therefore remains fluid.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The Philippines depends heavily on imported fuel and on international maritime trade. Serious disruption around Bab el-Mandeb can lengthen shipping routes, increase freight and insurance costs, and add pressure to global oil and refined-fuel prices.

For Filipino consumers and businesses, the main transmission risks are higher fuel and transport costs, more expensive imported goods and renewed inflation pressure. Those effects are risks rather than guaranteed outcomes and depend on how long the disruption lasts and whether commercial shipping can continue safely.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: It is not yet established that Houthi forces control or can close the entire Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The confirmed development is their capture of Perim Island and advances along the nearby Yemeni coast.

It also remains unclear how long the Houthis will hold the island, whether Yemeni government forces will mount a successful counteroffensive, and whether Saudi Arabia, the United States or other regional actors will intervene directly.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for verified changes in commercial vessel traffic through Bab el-Mandeb, any counteroffensive for Perim or Dhubab, new attacks on merchant or energy infrastructure, Saudi or U.S. military responses, and further movement in global oil and refined-fuel prices.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.
